questions.knowledge_point: Finding Solutions of Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm: Advanced Cases
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{4x} & ={3}^{1-x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{4x}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{1-x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

$$
4x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)=(1-x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =(1-x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ 4x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ 4x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ x(4\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ x & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{x-2} & ={7}^{3-2x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{x-2}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({7}^{3-2x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives

$$
(x-2)\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)=(3-2x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(7).
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =(3-2x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(7) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)-2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(7) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(7) & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)) & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(7) \\ x & =\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Solutions of Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x+2} & ={2}^{x+3} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x+2}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x+3})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
x+2=\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x+3}).
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
x+2=(x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2 & =(x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ x+2 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ x-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-2 \\ x(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)) & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-2 \\ x & =\frac{3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-2}{1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Solutions of Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{2x-2} & =2\cdot {9}^{x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2x-2}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\cdot {9}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
2x-2=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\cdot {9}^{x}).
$$

Next, we use the power and product laws of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-2 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+\operatorname{ln}⁡({9}^{x}) \\ 2x-2 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-2 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) \\ 2x-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) & =2+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ x(2-\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)) & =2+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ x & =\frac{2+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}{2-\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{5x-1} & ={7}^{3-x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{5x-1}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({7}^{3-x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}(5x-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =(3-x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(5x-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =(3-x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(7) \\ 5x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(7) \\ 5x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+x\operatorname{ln}⁡(7) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(7) \\ x(5\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(7) \\ x & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)}{5\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)}\end{aligned}
$$
